summary: This article covers the difference between renewable sources that naturally replenish, like sunlight, wind, and water, and nonrenewable sources, like oil, coal, and gas, that take millions of years to form.
introduce: Write “Alike” and “Different” at the top of a T-chart on the board and ask students to compare two school subjects in one minute. Explain that “Renewable vs Nonrenewable Energy” asks them to make the same kind of comparison.

keyTerms.def: formed from the remains of ancient plants or animals buried for millions of years
a material that is burned or used to produce energy
to fill something back up or make it full again

challengeTerms.def: having a limited amount or size
able to be continued for a long time without running out or causing serious harm
to add different kinds of something instead of relying on just one

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that countries should use more renewable energy, even if it costs more right now? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain the difference between renewable and nonrenewable energy and why that difference matters.
struggling: Pre-teach fossil, fuel, and replenish with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers fill in a T-chart of alike and different with sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use finite, sustainable, and diversify in a short paragraph that compares two ideas from the article and explain which difference matters most.
